page: Amazon Web Services t3a.micro is a burstable, entry-level instance within the General Purpose family, hosted on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The virtual machine provides 2 burstable vCPUs mapped to 1 physical AMD EPYC 7571 core operating at a base frequency of 2.2 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Hardware features include 8 MB of L3 cache alongside instruction support for AVX, AES-NI, and SHA extensions. Memory capacity is configured at 1.0 GB of DDR4 RAM running at 3 GHz, allocating 0.5 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include dedicated GPUs or local instance storage, and baseline network throughput is rated at 0 Gbps with burst capabilities.

Benchmark results place the instance in the entry-level performance tier, reflecting its constrained resources and shared CPU model. In CPU workloads, stress-ng registers 585.39 for single-core and 590.09 for multi-core compute, both falling into the lower 10 percent of evaluated systems. PassMark CPU overall scores reached 1863.86, with cryptographic tasks measuring 1613.71. Uncached large-block DDR4 memory throughput records 20.79 GB/sec read and 12.21 GB/sec write. In application tests, Redis achieved 1.2 million SET operations per second, and static web serving throughput reached 1.48 GB/sec.

The t3a.micro instance delivers low absolute operational expenditure by sharing underlying physical host resources, but sustained resource saturation remains limited by the burstable allocation model and minimal 1.0 GB memory footprint. Consequently, it is best suited for low-traffic web serving, lightweight microservices, configuration testbeds, and background automation scripts that experience intermittent rather than continuous compute demand.
